page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highmem-192-metal is a bare-metal server instance featuring 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 4.0 GHz, the platform includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside comprehensive hardware instruction support such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). As a non-virtualized bare-metal offering, hypervisor overhead is eliminated entirely.

Memory provisioning is substantial, offering 1536.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, providing a memory allocation of 8.0 GB per physical core (or 8 GB per vCPU across the hyper-threaded layout). The system includes no local disk storage and zero integrated GPUs, relying exclusively on network-attached storage architectures and CPU-based computational execution.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate superior parallel compute and memory throughput. The server achieved top-tier performance in multi-core stress-ng (160,631.15) and PassMark CPU metrics (125,054.48), alongside top-tier database operations (36,549.72) and Redis SET throughput reaching 181.93 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth highlights uncached read throughput of 464.93 GB/sec and write throughput of 201.86 GB/sec. CPU-driven LLM inference also registers strong results across 7B and 70B parameter models, capitalizing on Intel AMX vector execution.

With 1.5 TB of memory and 192 dedicated execution threads, this bare-metal profile is structured for high-density enterprise memory-bound workloads. Primary applications include massive in-memory caching layers, SAP HANA and large-scale relational databases, compute-heavy Clang software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based large language model inference.
